newsitem.title: USA: Just another restful jog on the beach for Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Just another restful jog on the beach for Clinton.

text.p: It was just another restful run on the beach for President Bill Clinton on Thursday morning.
On one side a woman named Valerie Parker was shouting at the president: "You're a draft-dodging, yellow-bellied liar!"

Running alongside him a man named Mark Skousen was complaining about his tax burden. And a cluster of reporters was yelling questions about what he knew about Russian President Boris Yeltsin's firing of his powerful security chief, Alexander Lebed. He ignored them all.

Parker, 32, of Bloomington, Illinois, gave Clinton a fiery, 10-minute tongue-lashing as he ended his run and walked along the beach cooling down near the Hotel del Coronado, where he spent the night after his second debate with Republican challenger Bob Dole on Wednesday night.

"You're a disgrace to the office of the presidency, to your gender, and to this nation. You're a draft-dodging, yellow-bellied liar. How can you act like you're a feminist when you have sexually harrassed?" she demanded.

Secret Service agents stood between the woman and Clinton and talked to her but did not try to stop her tirade. The president largely ignored the shouts but at one point gave the woman a casual salute, a thumbs-up, and said, "Thank you."
"How do you sleep at night, Mr. President? How come you don't feel Dole's pain?" she said.
When Renatte Adler of San Diego, holding a one-year-old child, tried to get Parker to quiet down, Parker yelled at her: "Oh shut up. Go get an abortion."
Adler said afterward: "I told her Clinton was for the children."
Other beach bystanders finally drowned out Parker. "Yay, Mr. President. Thanks for everything. Keep up the good work. We love you," one shouted.

Meanwhile Clinton was engaged in a long chat with Skousen, who told reporters later that he supported the Libertarian Party and its candidate for president, Harry Brown. Skousen, of Winter Park, Florida, was jogging on the beach himself and joined up with the president.
"He said 'How are you?' and I said, 'I could be better. My tax burden is real high.'"
Skousen heard Parker's tirade and said of Clinton's reaction: "It really didn't seem to bother him very much."
Clinton seemed to relish the conversation with Skousen. They chatted for a while after Clinton finished his exercise.
Asked if he watched the debate, Skousen said he did not. He was watching the baseball playoff game won by the Atlanta Braves, 3-1, over the St. Louis Cardinals.
